metadata.description: Structured ruleset for real-time barbell movement analysis combining joint safety constraints, execution standards, and no-rep detection.

angle_convention_details.hip_flexion: 0 = standing upright, increases with bending forward
angle_convention_details.shoulder_abduction: 0 = arm at side, increases with arm raising laterally
angle_convention_details.ankle_dorsiflexion: 0 = foot perpendicular to tibia, increases as shin moves forward
angle_convention_details.lumbar_flexion: 0 = neutral lordosis, increases with forward rounding
angle_convention_details.trunk_lean: 0 = perfectly vertical, increases with forward lean
angle_convention_details.knee_valgus: 0 = neutral frontal plane alignment, increases with inward collapse
angle_convention_details.thoracic_kyphosis: measured as increase above individual resting value
angle_convention_details.posterior_pelvic_tilt: 0 = starting neutral position, increases with tuck under

joint_safety_constraints.description: Medial knee collapse during loaded movement. Strongest single predictor of ACL injury.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Combined valgus loading with anterior tibial translation and internal rotation leading to ACL strain/rupture.
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Hewett et al. 2005 AJSM: ACL-injured athletes had 8° greater knee abduction; valgus moment predicted injury at 73% sensitivity, 78% specificity.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Requires frontal-plane camera or 3D pose estimation. 2D sagittal view insufficient.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Knee extending beyond 0° at top of movement under barbell load.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Posterior capsule strain, cruciate ligament stress. 15° causes moderate posterolateral damage; 30° causes partial ACL avulsion (Fornalski 2008).
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Normal physiological hyperextension 0-5° males, 0-6° females. Under load, any hyperextension beyond 5° is concerning.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Measured at lockout phase only. Use 0° = full extension convention where negative = hyperextension.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Deep knee flexion under barbell load. Generally safe but relevant for PCL pathology and patellofemoral pain.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: PCL forces peak at maximum flexion. Patellofemoral compressive forces peak ~130° reaching ~8000N.
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Schoenfeld 2010: ACL forces decrease beyond 60°. 87% of studies confirm deep squats do not increase injury risk.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Flag only if user profile indicates PCL or PFP history.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Hip flexion approaching anatomical limit causing posterior pelvic tilt (butt wink) and lumbar load transfer.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: When hip flexion reaches bony end-range (100-120° depending on anatomy), pelvis tilts posteriorly, transferring compressive and shear forces to lumbar discs.

optimal.note: Within normal ROM for most individuals

warning.note: Approaching end-range, monitor for pelvic tilt

joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Full-depth squats require ~120° hip flexion. Butt wink onset at 100-120° varies by acetabular depth, femoral neck angle, and version.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Must be evaluated in conjunction with lumbar_flexion and posterior_pelvic_tilt rules.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Asymmetric lateral pelvic shift during bilateral movements.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Unilateral overloading of lumbar facets, SI joint dysfunction, compensatory patterns.
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Lateral pelvic shift asymmetry exceeding 10% of ROM between sides is clinically meaningful.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Requires frontal-plane camera. Compare left vs right hip displacement from midline.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Insufficient ankle dorsiflexion causing compensatory lumbar flexion during squatting.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Below 15° dorsiflexion, compensatory lumbar flexion can reach 95% of maximum — dangerous substitution pattern.
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Normal ROM 15-20° non-weight-bearing. Full ATG squats demand 33-35° ± 5.5° (Hemmerich 2006).
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Flag athletes <15° as requiring heel elevation. Best measured during calibration phase.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Excessive shoulder abduction during bench press increasing subacromial impingement and AC joint loading.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Above 80° abduction, supraspinatus tendon compressed between humeral head and acromion. Combined with end-range external rotation at bottom of bench press, maximally stresses anterior glenohumeral ligament — primary mechanism for labral tears and pec major rupture.
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Noteboom et al. 2024 Frontiers Physiology: 90° abduction significantly increased glenohumeral superior shear and AC joint loading vs 45° and 70°.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Requires frontal or oblique camera angle. Difficult to measure from pure sagittal view.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Elbow extending beyond 0° at lockout under barbell load.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Risk to anterior capsule, olecranon stress fracture, collateral ligament strain.
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Normal physiological hyperextension 5-10° in some individuals. UCL tolerates ~30-35 Nm valgus torque before failure (Morrey & An 1983).
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Measured at lockout phase. Negative values indicate hyperextension beyond 0°.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Excessive wrist extension during barbell pressing or squatting.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Compressive load transmitted through extended wrist misaligns force vector off radius/ulna axis, increasing carpal and TFCC stress.

front_rack.note: Inherently stressful position at or beyond normal ROM. Monitor but do not flag as violation.

joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Normal extension ROM 60-75°. Under heavy load, bar should rest over radius/ulna axis near neutral.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Wrist keypoints often occluded by barbell. Low confidence expected.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Lumbar spine rounding under compressive barbell load — primary disc herniation mechanism.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Repeated flexion under compressive load herniates discs (McGill). At max flexion, spinal tolerance drops 30× (263 vs 8253 cycles). Flexion-relaxation phenomenon at 80-90% max ROM transfers all load to passive structures.

optimal.note: McGill recommends <50% of max ROM under load

joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Callaghan & McGill 2001: herniations at 5000-9500 cycles at higher loads. Gallagher 2005: max flexion = 30× reduction in cycle tolerance. Coached lifters maintain 22-26° perceived as neutral.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Measured as deviation from individual's calibrated neutral. Hip-to-shoulder vector vs vertical is a proxy.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Posterior pelvic tilt at bottom of squat causing lumbar kyphosis under load.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: End-range lumbar flexion under compressive load. McGill identifies last 2-3° of ROM as most injurious zone.

critical.note: With visible lumbar kyphosis under load

joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Butt wink beyond 10-20° approaches lumbar neutral zone boundary. Onset depends on individual hip anatomy (100-120° hip flexion).
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Measured as change from starting pelvic position to bottom position. Requires tracking pelvis orientation.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Increase in thoracic kyphosis beyond resting baseline during loaded movements.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Upper back rounding increases compensatory lumbar extension and shoulder stress. Indicates upper back strength deficit.
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Normal standing thoracic kyphosis 40-45° (Neumann 2010). Only 20-25° of available extension. Overhead lockout requires reducing to ~15-20° total.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Measured relative to individual baseline, not absolute. Requires calibration.

joint_safety_constraints.description: Cervical spine deviation from neutral under axial barbell load.
joint_safety_constraints.injury_mechanism: Hyperextension compresses posterior facet joints/discs. Flexion stretches posterior ligaments under compression. Lateral flexion creates asymmetric disc loading.
joint_safety_constraints.evidence: Neutral = slight chin tuck maintaining lordosis, gaze 10-15° below horizontal.
joint_safety_constraints.measurement_notes: Any plane deviation measured. Ear-to-shoulder vector vs vertical is a reasonable proxy.

depth_requirement.rule: Top surface of legs at hip joint must be lower than top of knees

proxy_angle.note: Exact angle varies with anthropometry. Hip crease below kneecap is the visual standard.

red_light_causes.description: Hip crease not below top of knees
red_light_causes.detection_method: Compare hip_joint_y to knee_joint_y in sagittal view
Detect negative vertical velocity of bar/hip after ascent begins

red_light_causes.description: Failure to achieve full knee extension at completion
Stepping or lateral foot movement (rocking ball-to-heel permitted)
red_light_causes.detection_method: Track foot keypoint horizontal displacement >5cm from start position

red_light_causes.description: Elbow contact with legs providing support
red_light_causes.detection_method: Proximity check between elbow and knee keypoints during ascent

descent_requirement.rule: Elbows must be lowered so underside of both elbow joints is level with or below top of each shoulder joint

proxy_angle.note: 2026 rule addition — enforces minimum descent depth beyond chest touch

red_light_causes.description: Bar heaves or sinks into chest after being motionless
red_light_causes.detection_method: Detect downward bar velocity after pause period begins

red_light_causes.description: Any downward bar movement after press command
red_light_causes.detection_method: Detect negative vertical bar velocity during press phase

red_light_causes.description: Buttocks losing contact with bench during press
red_light_causes.detection_method: Track hip keypoint vertical displacement relative to bench surface
Track foot keypoint vertical displacement from floor baseline

red_light_causes.description: Arms not evenly extended at completion
red_light_causes.detection_method: Compare left vs right elbow extension angle; flag if difference > 10°

red_light_causes.description: Elbows not lowered to shoulder level before press
red_light_causes.detection_method: Compare elbow_y to shoulder_y; flag if elbow remains above shoulder

bar_path.description: Slight arc from lower chest back toward face during press

lockout_requirements.shoulder_rule: Front bundle of deltoid behind imaginary vertical projection of bar

red_light_causes.description: Any downward bar movement before reaching final position
red_light_causes.detection_method: Detect negative vertical bar velocity before lockout achieved

red_light_causes.description: Failure to lock knees at lockout
Failure to stand erect with shoulders back
red_light_causes.detection_method: Trunk lean > 10° from vertical at lockout OR shoulder_x forward of bar_x

red_light_causes.description: Supporting bar on thighs during ascent with upward leg movement
red_light_causes.detection_method: Detect bar resting on thigh (bar velocity near zero while hip extending) with knee re-bend

red_light_causes.description: Any foot movement during the lift
red_light_causes.detection_method: Track foot keypoint displacement > 3cm from start position

Hands placed inside knees (sumo deadlift not permitted)

Elbows not clearly in front of bar in rack position

clean_and_jerk.critical_rule: If any portion receives no-rep, entire rep must be repeated from floor. Cannot reattempt jerk from rack.

Arms, hips, or knees not fully extended overhead
For split jerk, feet not returned to parallel position before lowering bar
Bar not over or behind midline at lockout
Bar pauses or rests at shoulder level (becomes a clean-and-jerk)

fatigue_detection.description: Rep-to-rep drift detection comparing each rep to the first rep of a set. Fatigue-induced form degradation is the primary injury mechanism in trained lifters.

alert_thresholds.description: Lumbar flexion increases >10-15° from first rep
Knee valgus increases >5° from first rep
Trunk forward lean increases >10° from first rep
Bar path horizontal deviation increases >2cm from first rep
Squat depth varies >5° knee flexion between consecutive reps
Bar velocity drops >20-30% from first rep
Rapid, discontinuous increase in lumbar flexion — precedes disc injury under load
alert_thresholds.detection: Rate of change of lumbar flexion exceeds 2 standard deviations from mean rep-to-rep change

sagittal_view.position: perpendicular to movement plane at hip height

frontal_view.position: directly in front or behind at hip height

calibration.description: Individual baseline ROM assessment before applying population thresholds. Population thresholds are accurate for ~80% of training population.
calibration.individual_variation_note: Hip and thoracic anatomy can shift optimal ranges by 15-20° in either direction.
